Map exploration interactions

The 2D map uses one dispatcher for exploration. Layers supply targets; the shared content sheet presents them. Drawing, measurement, and planning retain their own gestures. The separate 3D replay map does not use this dispatcher.

On this page
  • Small dispatcher contract
  • Lifetime and presentation
  • Public trail details

Small dispatcher contract

mapInteractionDecision.ts defines the target union, semantic identity, pointer/touch tolerance, deduplication, and presentation decisions. mapInteractionCoordinator.ts owns click lifetime and incremental source state. Neither module imports Vue or MapLibre at runtime.

Map consumers register with registerConsumer, which returns a cleanup function. The controller exposes registerMapInteractionConsumer for additional map components; registrations can precede map initialization and survive renderer recreation until their component calls cleanup. Map children can use useMapInteractionConsumer to access the provided dispatcher and clean up on unmount:

  • A local consumer collects candidates synchronously from the captured click.
  • An asynchronous consumer supplies a cancellable provider with a bounded timeout.
  • Either consumer can declare eligibility against the captured context.

Registration and cleanup invalidate an existing interaction. The main map adapter registers the fixed POI, track-point, photo, filtered-track, Swiss-route, and enabled Waymarked activity consumers. This is a candidate dispatcher; existing type-specific handlers still open details and photo collections. Adding a consumer does not require another map click listener or presentation surface.

useMapInteractions.ts binds the dispatcher to map events and existing handlers. useMainMapController.ts binds invalidation to tool ownership, track filter revision, media scope, and layer settings. Map2DRenderer.vue hosts one exploration BottomSheet and a separate foreground GPS detail BottomSheet; MapTargetChooser.vue starts with a bounded All overview. mapTargetCategories.ts groups presentation by target kind and trail source, without changing consumer registration or candidate identity. Waymarked activities share one category, as do Swiss route layers. Unknown registered sources remain accessible through their own category.

All is the initial chooser view. A ten-row preview budget shares space across categories, with at most three targets in each category, followed by a counted more row. Small sets within those bounds show every target directly. Categories with results, pending lookups or lookup issues stay reachable through wrapping, persistent chips. A summary or chip opens 20 targets per page, with every returned target accessible. Photo counts distinguish collection targets from individual photos. Pending, unavailable, and cancelled categories remain visible; completed empty categories are hidden.

Available screen distances rank an initial batch. GPS peers use available server proximity distances, then canonical recording time, newest first. Localized display dates are never parsed; equal or unavailable values keep supplied order. Late arrivals preserve previews, category order, the current page, and focus. A new click resets navigation; selected content remains mounted through Back to results and reopening its result row. Category controls appear only in the chooser; selected details use the shared sheet's header Back action. The sheet's optional backLabel and back event keep navigation with the caller. Track details emit the same generic event without knowing their return destination. GPS rows share TrackChoiceRow with the photo activity picker. The row contains a title and compact activity/date/distance/ascent facts, plus available photo counts. Canonical timestamps and measurements are formatted reactively through the app's locale/unit helpers; total lengthMeters is distinct from hit distanceMeters. TrackChoiceFacts provides the compact metric badges for archived GPS rows. Proximity distances are used for ordering and are not displayed in these map lists. Its lazy cached TrackShapePreview appears on the right, before the chevron, only when the list container is at least 40 rem wide. A track icon remains on the left at every width. The sketch uses a subdued theme-aware blue, a 1.75 px stroke and no opacity fade. Mouse/pen hover and keyboard focus reuse the existing track-highlight source without changing selection, viewport or URL. Leaving the row, hiding the chooser, changing the click or closing it clears the preview while retaining the selected track highlight. Routine geometry refreshes retain an eligible preview. Touch does not preview.

The chooser uses a fixed shared-sheet detent capped at 30 rem or 60% of the viewport, whichever is smaller. Its height stays constant through source updates, category changes and paging. Manual dragging and maximization remain available. GPS details open at the expanded 92vh detent and standard width on desktop. On mobile they maximize to 100dvh and full width. GPS details use a separate foreground sheet. The dispatcher stays mounted at its unchanged height, with its chooser inert while covered. Foreground opening covers at least the underlying sheet's height; explicit detail resizing is still allowed. Back, Close and browser Back hide GPS details and reveal the unchanged dispatcher, preserving its category, page and manual size. Retained GPS content stays mounted for reopening. GPS Close uses the sheet's deferClose and close-request contract to request the same return navigation as Back. The panel closes only after navigation commits. Pending or failed returns preserve its size and maximized state; Close can be retried. Drag-to-close restores the pre-drag height while waiting for navigation. Other detail types retain the dispatcher's current panel size. The chooser adds no scroll container or independent height calculation. Standalone GPS details also open expanded. When a tool such as Statistics or Filter opens GPS details, route synchronization keeps the originating tool open underneath. The return target retains its navigation state; returning reveals the existing panel without reopening it.

The GPS sheet shares its layout with nested media viewers only in map exploration. Statistics, Filter and direct-link media viewers keep their own viewport centering and size presets. Ordinary media viewing leaves the GPS sheet's height unchanged; the compact background detent is enabled only while 3D replay is active.

Lifetime and presentation

Every accepted exploration click opens Choose what to see here on All, even with zero or one candidate. Only explicit row selection opens details. Pending categories show a spinner and one skeleton row while known hits remain clickable. Completed empty categories have no chip or All-list group. If the selected category finishes empty, the chooser returns to All and focuses its chip. A confirmed empty location shows “Nothing found here”; unavailable and cancelled sources remain distinct.

Filtered track proximity and route identification settle independently. GPS lookup starts existing ID and nearby-media lookups in parallel. IDs and processing notices appear immediately; optional facts enrich existing rows without changing their order or selection. Media facts have a bounded three-second timeout; failure keeps GPS IDs and processing notices without reporting missing facts as zero. Late hits append without changing category navigation, visible ordering or selected details. A point's parent track remains an action of the point rather than another overlap row. Photo and cluster taps publish the primary collection and one captured Map view at tap choice directly under Photos. Fully known equal ID sets are deduplicated; incomplete cluster membership retains both scopes. Collection counts do not sum overlapping photo totals. Each row opens the existing viewer directly, with no secondary photo chooser or associated-GPS lookup in this dispatcher flow. Viewport selection uses captured IDs without expanding cluster leaves. Both scopes carry the original map bounds for the viewer's overview; legacy callers retain their existing collection chooser and current-map fallback.

Full GPS details use the existing /track/:id route. useMapInteractionTrackRoute keeps the return context in the caller, separate from the dispatcher and detail components. Header Back and browser Back restore retained chooser navigation; Forward restores the same selected content. Reload or a direct link uses standalone track routing, with Back returning to an available overview or the map. Only track identity goes in the URL, and superseded or rejected navigation cannot restore an old selection. Points and photo/POI/public-route results retain the map URL until the user explicitly opens full GPS details.

Each accepted click captures coordinates, actual pointer/touch/pen input, filter revision, media scope, and eligibility. Requests check both interaction identity and cancellation. Manual movement cancels unfinished discovery but retains the original click, collected targets, and selected detail loads. Programmatic focus movement preserves discovery. Double-click zoom skips the second exploration click and clears only the gesture's interaction.

useMapInteractionVisibility listens to the shared sheet's actual layout. Once its opening geometry settles, an occluded click gets the minimum vertical pixel pan needed to leave 32 px above the chooser. Zoom, bearing and pitch stay fixed; the original discovery context is retained. A clear marker requires no movement. Each click gets one attempt, including clicks while the chooser stays open. Manual movement, early sheet resizing, selection and close cancel that attempt; late results, category changes and returning from details do not move the camera.

Providers time out after 15 seconds. Failure, timeout, cancelled discovery, incomplete track processing, and confirmed empty results remain distinct. One failed consumer does not discard other results. Close, a new click, invalidation, style replacement, and disposal prevent late responses from reopening content. Ending retained results also discards GPS details hidden by Back to results; they must not reopen as standalone content. Visible GPS details may continue on their standalone route when the discovery context is invalidated.

For retained photo-cluster targets, the media overlay keeps the original source tree until the interaction ends. Viewport refreshes queue their latest data during that interval. This preserves collection identity and pagination after panning; no complete leaf expansion is needed. Invalidation closes a photo collection whose pagination depended on that retained tree.

Public trail details

waymarkedTrailProvider.ts captures the click tolerance through public map unprojection before any request. It intersects the frozen Mercator footprint with Waymarked Trails geometry tiles and resolves every matched top-level relation through list/by_ids. This avoids the area endpoint's 100-result cap. Adjacent tiles and repeated segments are deduplicated. Metadata requests use batches rather than limiting the number of targets.

Geometry requests are limited to 16 tiles per activity and use a bounded five-minute memory cache. Wider clicks show Zoom in to identify Waymarked Trails routes, with unavailable status rather than an empty result. Names, references, itineraries, known network labels, and official route-page links appear in the existing flow. swissRouteDetails.ts fetches htmlPopup only after a Swiss feature is selected. It extracts the published SchweizMobil stage and full-route URLs from inert markup. Stage details is the primary link when present. Unnamed swisstopo segments expose available classification and a Swiss map link; missing names or homepages are not invented. Selected detail requests have a timeout and interaction/selection guards, and ordinary panning preserves them.

The grouped chooser has no archive actions. Download and 3D replay remain in selected archived track content. MapOverlayDetails.vue displays only external route fields and validated links.

Selected routes use a dedicated detail layout in that same sheet: a wrapped route name, activity icon, metadata card and primary external action. The first available validated link is primary, with Swiss stage details preferred. MapPoiDetails.vue presents mapped place types with their existing category icons and colors, plus elevation when available. Its pure presentation helper also supplies the sheet header icon. Both use the shared compact desktop width and content fitting. These panels add no lookups or extra sheets.

API contracts: Waymarked geometry, route listings, Swiss HTML popups.
